audit.whatIsWrong: Five of seven full-layer sides disagreed with the content layer and packet levelChart. Full read Orianna/Orianna/Orianna/Skill/Skill/Skill/Ryze; content and packet read Orianna/Skill/Skill/Orianna/Orianna/Skill/Orianna — including the two-item row, which the full layer gave to Ryze while its own why described Orianna winning teamfights.
audit.why: 49.4% over 1324 games. Levels 2-3 are a real fight as his rune chain comes online; 4-6 swing to Orianna because Rune Prison only roots a Flux target and Realm Warp is not lane pressure; first item is even on his rune stacks; two-plus items is Orianna's grouped-fight row.
audit.corrected: Rows 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6 moved to the content layer's verdict, with whys 1-5 rewritten in the same group. phases[6].why already described Orianna winning late, so the side now matches the sentence under it.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why gave the generic 'your lane presence doubles' line and breakdown.spikes repeated it; neither said what happens at 6 in this specific lane.
audit.why: Realm Warp is 180/160/140 at 3000 range and teleports allies near a portal — a rotation tool, not lane pressure. That is why level 6 belongs to Orianna here: Shockwave threatens a kill and his ultimate does not answer it.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why and breakdown.spikes rewritten around the 180-second portal being map utility rather than a lane answer.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page treats Rune Prison as an unconditional 'point-blank root'. It is not one.
audit.why: Riot's text for Rune Prison (W, 11/10.5/10/9.5/9, 615) says it damages and slows, and roots instead only if the target already has Flux on it. Spell Flux (E, 3.5/3.25/3/2.75/2.5, 615) is what applies Flux and it spreads to nearby enemies. Overload (Q, 5s, 1000) is reset by his other basic abilities and charges runes, with a move-speed burst at two runes. So the whole lane reduces to one rule the page never states: dodge the orb and the cage is a slow, not a root.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t, winCon and the do/don't bodies now say the root is conditional on Spell Flux and give the 11s, 3.5s and 5s cooldowns.
sources: enemyKit W/E/Q text, cooldowns and ranges

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns named the ability and gave no number.
audit.why: Rune Prison at 11s rank 1 is the window you step into; Spell Flux at 3.5s is why you cannot simply wait Flux out.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with all three of his lane cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer says three times that Orianna out-ranges Ryze's 'short-cast' or 'short-range' Overload — whys[0], early, and spikes[0].
audit.why: Overload is listed at 1000 range against Command: Attack's 815, so the range advantage runs the other way for that spell. Orianna's real reach advantage is over Rune Prison and Spell Flux, both 615.
audit.corrected: All three rewritten to the reach advantage that actually exists (815 against 615) and to the Flux-conditional root, without changing which side wins any row.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d, dosFull[2].d and dontsFull[2].d were foreign strings pasted under unrelated titles.
audit.why: The titles promise wave contacts, auto-weaving and Shockwave discipline; the bodies talked about trades and ball position.
audit.corrected: All three rewritten to match their titles.

notes: Two real errors fixed here beyond the templates. First, the page called Rune Prison a 'point-blank root' throughout; Riot's text says it damages and slows, and roots only if the target already has Flux on it — that conditional is the entire matchup and it was absent from every field. Second, the content layer claimed three times (whys[0], early, spikes[0]) that Orianna out-ranges Ryze's Overload; Overload is 1000 range against Command: Attack's 815, so the claim is backwards. The real reach edge is 815 against his 615 W and E, and all three strings now say that instead — no chart row changes as a result. Full-layer sides disagreed with the content layer on rows 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6, including a two-item row marked Ryze above a why describing Orianna winning teamfights; content was right and only the full sides move. phases[N].rating untouched: the scale is inconsistent across this dataset.
